verdicts.rule: '=' WITH HELP. Any help spelling with an explicit '=' value errors: "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<VALUE>'", value in Python repr single quotes. Exit 2.
verdicts.note: Reproduced --help=1 / --h=1 / --he=1 / --hel=1 / -h=1. Additional boundary cases that follow the same rule: `./test8_executable --help=` and `-h=` and `--h=` -> "ignored explicit argument ''" (empty repr, two quote chars); `-h==` -> "ignored explicit argument '='" (split on first '=' only). Also confirmed this error is NOT pre-scanned: `./test8_executable -h --help=1` -> exit 0, help printed, because the earlier -h action fires first.

verdicts.rule: '=' ON AN UNKNOWN OPTION. Whole token including '=1' echoed as one unrecognized token; 'required' wins if a required option is unset.
verdicts.note: Reproduced --unknown=1 and --pz=1 in both configurations. Also `./test8_executable --payload x --secret y --s=q --pz` -> 'unrecognized arguments: --pz' (the valid abbreviation --s=q is consumed, only the unknown token is echoed).

Reproduced all six of their cases. Additional: `./test8_executable --pz x --secret y` -> required --payload (the extras --pz and x are silently dropped from the message); `./test8_executable -- -h` -> required --payload, --secret. Caveat already implied elsewhere: both are outranked by ambiguous-option (pre-scan) and by 'expected one argument' (raised mid-scan).

verdicts.rule: UNRECOGNIZED ARGUMENTS. 'unrecognized arguments: ' + leftovers joined by a single space in original argv order; '--' itself included; empty-string argv element contributes an empty token. Exit 2.
verdicts.note: Could not find any reordering counterexample. Verified argv-order preservation with mixed positional/unknown-option interleavings: `./test8_executable gamma --alpha --payload a --secret b --beta` -> 'gamma --alpha --beta'; `./test8_executable --alpha --payload a --secret b --beta gamma` -> '--alpha --beta gamma'; `./test8_executable --payload a --secret b extra -- more` -> 'extra -- more'; `-- -- extra` -> '-- -- extra'. Trailing-space claim verified byte-wise: `./test8_executable --payload a --secret b '' 2>/tmp/e` then `od -An -c /tmp/e` ends '... a r g u m e n t s :  (space) \n'; with two empty strings it ends with two spaces before \n. Also '-', '---', '-p', '-1', '-1x' all land in extras verbatim.

verdicts.rule: MISSING VALUE / VALUE LOOKS LIKE AN OPTION. Triggered when the option is the last token, or when the next token starts with '-' and is not a negative number. '-1' IS accepted.
verdicts.note:
The 'starts with - and is not a negative number' predicate mispredicts at least three input classes (all exit 0, all should be errors under the stated rule):
  `./test8_executable --payload - --secret y` -> exit 0, {'data': '-'}  (a lone '-' is always a value)
  `./test8_executable --payload '-x y' --secret y` -> exit 0, {'data': '-x y'}  (token contains a space and matches no option prefix -> value)
  `./test8_executable --payload '- x' --secret y` -> exit 0, {'data': '- x'}; `--payload '-1 '` -> {'data': '-1 '}; `--payload ' -1'` -> {'data': ' -1'}
  `./test8_executable --payload -.5 --secret y` -> exit 0, {'data': '-.5'}  ('-.5' has no digit before the dot yet is still 'negative-number-like')
Corrected predicate: the following token IS consumed as a value iff it is the empty string, OR its first char is not '-', OR it is exactly '-', OR it matches /^-\d+$/ or /^-\d*\.\d+$/, OR (it matches no registered option/prefix AND contains a space). Otherwise -> 'argument <CANONICAL>: expected one argument'. Confirmed errors: `--payload -1a`, `--payload -secret`, `--payload --`, `--payload -h`, `--payload -x`, and bare trailing `--payload`/`--p`/`--s`.
Also the precedence claim needs one exception: this error does NOT beat the ambiguous-option pre-scan — `./test8_executable --payload --=1` -> exit 2 'ambiguous option: --=1 could match --help, --payload, --secret'.
The canonical-name part IS confirmed: `--p` and `--payload x --secret y --p` both report 'argument --payload: expected one argument'.

verdicts.rule: HELP WINS OVER MISSING-REQUIRED AND OVER UNKNOWN OPTIONS. If -h/--help/--h/--he/--hel appears anywhere and is REACHED in the left-to-right scan, help prints to stdout and exit 0.
verdicts.note:
Falsified by the ambiguous-option pre-scan, which runs over ALL argv tokens before any action executes, so an ambiguous token anywhere (even far to the RIGHT of -h) kills help:
  `./test8_executable -h '--='` -> EXIT=2, stdout EMPTY, stderr 'usage: ...\ntest8_executable: error: ambiguous option: --= could match --help, --payload, --secret'
  `./test8_executable --help '--=1'` -> EXIT=2, same class of error
  `./test8_executable -h -h '--='` -> EXIT=2 ambiguous
  `./test8_executable -h --payload=x --secret=y '--=q'` -> EXIT=2 'ambiguous option: --=q could match ...'
  `./test8_executable --payload x --secret y -h '--=zzz'` -> EXIT=2 ambiguous
Corrected rule: FIRST classify every token left-to-right until a bare '--'; if any of them is an ambiguous long-option prefix, error immediately (exit 2). ONLY THEN execute actions left-to-right, where -h/--help/--h/--he/--hel/-hX fires help and exits 0, beating missing-required and unknown options. Their other listed cases all reproduce: `--bogus -h`, `-h --bogus`, `--payload x -h`, `--bogus=1 -h`, `--help --payload`, `--payload x --help --secret`, `-h -- --payload`, `--payload x -h y` -> all exit 0 with the 164-byte help; `--payload -h`, `--help=1 -h` -> exit 2; `-- -h` -> exit 2 required error.

verdicts.rule: SHORT-OPTION CLUSTER '-hX'. '-h' + non-'-' chars fires help and exits 0; if the trailing char is '-' it errors with "ignored explicit argument '-'"; '-xh'/'-x' never fire help.
verdicts.note:
Direction is right but the error message is misstated for multi-char tails: the reported value is the ENTIRE remainder after '-h', not a single '-'.
  `./test8_executable -h-x` -> exit 2, "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '-x'"
  `./test8_executable -h--`  -> exit 2, "... ignored explicit argument '--'"
  `./test8_executable -h-h`  -> exit 2, "... ignored explicit argument '-h'"
Corrected rule: for a token '-h'+TAIL with no '=', if TAIL[0] is a prefix char ('-') the parser errors with "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<TAIL>'"; otherwise the whole TAIL is discarded and help fires (exit 0). Additional confirmations of the help branch: `-he`, `-h1`, `-hpayload`, and even `'-h '` (trailing space) all print the 164-byte help and exit 0 — note '-h ' fires help even though a space normally forces a token to be positional, because short-prefix matching happens before the space check. `-xh`/`-x` confirmed as plain extras.

Reproduced, plus mixed canonical/abbreviated repeats: `./test8_executable --payload a --p b --secret y` -> {'data': 'b'} (same token as their --payload a --payload b case); `./test8_executable --secret a --secret b --payload p` -> exit 0, signature differs from the --secret a variant, i.e. the LAST --secret wins too.

verdicts.rule: PROG NAME IS DYNAMIC: basename(argv[0]) in both the usage line and the 'PROG: error:' prefix.
verdicts.note: Stronger evidence than a copy: it tracks argv[0], not the on-disk file. `bash -c 'exec -a fakeprog /tmp/zz_renamed_prog --help'` -> 'usage: fakeprog [-h] --payload PAYLOAD --secret SECRET'; a symlink `/tmp/linkname_prog -> /tmp/zz_renamed_prog` -> 'usage: linkname_prog ...'; invoking via absolute path `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable` still yields prog 'test8_executable' (basename, not the full path).

verdicts.rule: WRAPPING WIDTH = COLUMNS - 2 (fallback 80 -> width 78); usage single-line for COLUMNS>=64, wraps for <=63; continuation indent 24; at COLUMNS=40 help column is 18 and the help text wraps; error line never wrapped.
verdicts.note:
Rule text is correct and I reproduced every part, BUT their pasted observedStdout for COLUMNS=40 (in this rule and in rule 3) is fabricated/wrong: it shows the options block unchanged. Real output of `COLUMNS=40 ./test8_executable --help`:
  options:
  -h, --help      show this help
                  message and exit
  --payload PAYLOAD
  --secret SECRET

(help column measured at 0-based 18 via awk index). Threshold re-verified: COLUMNS=61/62/63 wrap, 64/65 do not. Extra edges a JS port may want: COLUMNS=0, negative ('-5'), non-numeric ('abc') and empty all fall back to width 78 (identical 164-byte help); the layout saturates for small values — COLUMNS=1 through 17 all produce identical output (help text wrapped at 11 columns: 'show this'/'help'/'message and'/'exit'), COLUMNS=18 starts differing.

verdicts.rule: SUCCESS PATH. Exit 0, three stdout lines: token, Python dict repr of claims with single quotes, then {'alg': 'HS256', 'typ': 'JWT'}. Non-ASCII escaped as \uXXXX in the JWT but printed raw UTF-8 in the repr; tabs print as '\t'.
verdicts.note:
The 'single quotes' part is wrong for values containing an apostrophe — Python repr switches to double quotes:
  `./test8_executable --payload "it's" --secret s` -> line 2 is  {'data': "it's"}
  `./test8_executable --payload "both ' and \"" --secret s` -> line 2 is  {'data': 'both \' and "'}  (both quote kinds present -> single quotes with backslash-escaped apostrophe)
  `./test8_executable --payload 'say "hi"' --secret s` -> {'data': 'say "hi"'} (double quote alone does NOT change the delimiter)
Corrected rule for line 2/3 value rendering: use Python str repr — delimiter is ' unless the string contains ' and does not contain ", in which case it is "; inside a '-delimited string a literal ' is escaped as \'; \\ is always escaped as \\\\; \n/\r/\t render as the two-char escapes; other C0 controls render as \xNN (`--payload $'a\x01b'` -> {'data': 'a\x01b'}); printable non-ASCII is emitted raw UTF-8.
Everything else confirmed, plus astral characters in the JWT use UTF-16 surrogate escapes: `--payload '😀'` -> JWT payload segment decodes to {"data": "😀"} while the repr line prints the raw emoji bytes.
